strengths: Novel approach to addressing cumulative attention errors through retrospective output updates
Well-motivated problem identification with clear empirical evidence (Fig. 1b showing performance gap widening)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple benchmarks and thorough ablation studies
Rigorous theoretical overhead analysis (arithmetic intensity, memory footprint) with empirical validation
Practical improvements with minimal latency overhead (<1-2ms) and effective KV exposure gains (1.6×)
Clear presentation with effective visualizations and detailed algorithmic descriptions
Solid technical contribution building on existing non-eviction sparse attention methods
weaknesses: Key approximation (merging partial softmax across different Query representations) lacks rigorous theoretical justification despite empirical Q/K drift <5%
Highly inconsistent improvements across tasks (0% on GPQA-D, +0.5% on MMLU, +3.9% on GSM8K) without explanation of which factors determine success
Limited direct evidence that RetroAttention actually reduces cumulative attention errors - no comparison of attention output errors or hidden state drift before/after updates
Restricted evaluation scope: single model size (Llama 3.1-8B), limited context lengths (up to 256k), no evaluation on other architectures or larger models
Insufficient analysis of when retrospective updates might hurt or of task characteristics that lead to large/small performance gains
Hyperparameter sensitivity underexplored: window size w choice appears critical but practical guidance for new scenarios is missing
Missing comparisons with some recent baselines (RetrievalAttention, TokenSelect, ClusterKV) and no comparison with concurrent work (Sun et al. 2025)
The assumption of 'smooth QKV evolution' enabling approximate equivalence across consecutive steps needs deeper theoretical grounding

strengths: Novel retrospective attention refinement paradigm that breaks from fixed-output assumptions and effectively addresses cumulative errors during long generation
Rigorous motivational study (Section 2.2) with compelling empirical evidence that 15-20% of current KV entries are missed but relevant for past queries
Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple model sizes (8B-32B), architectures (Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek), and diverse benchmarks with consistent 3.9-5.6% average accuracy gains
Strong theoretical analysis establishing memory-bound behavior via arithmetic intensity, explaining negligible latency overhead despite 4-7% added computation
Thorough engineering with custom CUDA kernels, FlashInfer optimization, detailed kernel-level breakdown, and code release commitment enabling reproducibility
Clear quantification of effective KV exposure gains (1.17-1.60×) and saturation behavior analysis providing insight into performance limits
weaknesses: Query representation mismatch issue (Section C.2) incompletely addressed—assumes smooth QKV evolution across retrospective window validated only through L2 distance checks (<5%), lacking theoretical error bounds and main-paper prominence
Limited scope despite broad presentation: marginal improvements on long-input benchmarks (LONGBENCH), requires full KV cache in DRAM, and strongest results only for concatenated-generation scenarios
Concurrent work (Sun et al. 2025) addressing similar cumulative errors inadequately discussed—no empirical comparison despite methodological overlap, relegated to appendix
Performance saturation at w=8 suggests fundamental limitations; gains diminish quickly (4-7% first update), and throughput reduction of 3-7% (Table 6) contradicts 'negligible overhead' claims
Incomplete theoretical justification for softmax merging with evolved Queries; error propagation through layers not analyzed; approximation quality in memory-bound regimes under-explored
Moderate incremental novelty—retrospective refinement is novel but leverages established components (Quest selection, FlashAttention merging, output caching) without fundamental innovation

Experimental limitations: greedy decoding only, inconsistent model selection (DeepSeek-R1 only for reasoning), arbitrary hyperparameter choices (w=2 in main results), minimal gains on reasoning-intensive tasks (0% on GPQA-D)
